episodes.211368: A series of minor weather disturbances moved through the region from April 9th through the 11th. These combined with increased moisture to bring showers and storms to the region. With enough wind shear available in the atmosphere, some of these storms brought severe wind gusts to the region. Dry and windy conditions were in place on April 9th and that helped drive the spread of a wildfire known as The Smooth Eddy Incident which was over 500 acres. Additionally, the Purple Monster Wildfire would be sparked due to dry lightning in Oldham County on the evening of April 9th. That fire would go on to burn 1,911 acres.
episodes.211866: Clusters of severe storms developed across north central Kansas in the early evening before tracking southeast into the late evening hours towards portions of northeast Kansas. Storms produced large hail up to hen egg size (2 inches), wind damage to a barn and trees, and heavy rainfall up to 5 inches in Marshall county.
episodes.212394: Thunderstorms formed in far Northern California and Southern Oregon during the 2nd week of April. At least two storms became severe in the Eureka service area with hail reported in the Orleans area and strong wind gusts over the mountains.
episodes.212622: On the early evening of 4/9, enough surface convergence from a front was able to take advantage of 2000 J/kg CAPE with sufficient moisture for modest convection. With the strongest of the storms, 1 inch hail was reported.
episodes.213041: Scattered thunderstorms developed across portions of central Kansas during the afternoon and evening hours of April 9th. Large hail up to golf ball size were reported.

events.narrative: A severe thunderstorm developed over the Trinity Alps Wilderness and moved north over Orleans. Numerous reports of hail were received with pea to nickel sized hail generally reported. One report was received of 1 inch hail stones near the Orleans store. Hail was covering the ground in the community.
Ship Mountain RAWS reported a wind gust to 65 mph as thunderstorms moved through the area.
A public report of 1 inch hail.
